_law: RC-325, operator mandate 2026-08-09 (roughly the tenth instruction): ONE and only ONE producer for every field in this repository, Schwab leaf or derived. Many consumers are expected and correct. A consumer CARRIES the produced value; it never recomputes it. SCOPE REPAIR 2026-08-26 (RC-325): browser surfaces are production and are now enumerated by the gate (static/*.html, static/*.js, static/js/*.js). Before this, computing_sites quantified over Python alone, so a second implementation in the browser could not be counted and the FAIL condition was unreachable across runtimes. The law is ONE COMPUTATION repo-wide; the lock was one computation per-Python.
_why_this_file_exists: Every prior faucet lock was scoped to the surface failing in front of me: single_faucet_provenance sees 3 kl_* keys, phase2a_level_lock governs 19 level ids, and server.py emits 592 distinct payload keys. Enforcement over a domain requires the domain to be enumerated. This file IS that enumeration, and tools/check_one_producer.py quantifies over it.

_verdicts.PASS: registered field, exactly one computing site, and it is the declared producer
_verdicts.FAIL: registered field computed in two or more sites, or in a site that is not the declared producer
_verdicts.NOT_PROVEN: field not yet registered. ENFORCED as a one-way ratchet by tools/check_one_producer.py (not_proven_failures), which both violations() and the CLI apply, against the frozen name set in governance/one_producer_not_proven_baseline.txt. Registering a field always passes; only GROWTH of the unenforced remainder fails. CORRECTED 2026-08-26: this previously said the count was asserted by tests/test_one_producer_registry_v1.py, a file that had never existed in 1,796 commits, while violations() discarded not_proven entirely — so the remainder could and did drift (596 -> 604 in one session) behind a green seam.

_payload_surfaces_note: RC-325/SP-05: the files whose emitted fields are classified as registered or NOT_PROVEN. Declaring them makes their ABSENCE a fail-closed violation — the checker raises PayloadSurfaceMissing rather than reporting zero unresolved fields, because 'I could not look' must never read as 'there is nothing there'. A fixture repo that declares none is silent by design; this repo declares server.py and therefore cannot pass while it is missing.
_how_to_add_a_field: Name the field, the ONE module:function permitted to compute it, and the evidence you used to establish that it is the only one. Adding a field without deleting the competing sites is a FAIL, not a registration.

The prior generic inputs (gamma, openInterest, spot) false-matched math_probabilities.score_option_expression, whose only qualifying construct is `base += min(abs(gamma) * 10.0, 3.0)` — a scoring accumulation that mentions gamma but is NOT a $GEX derivation (no OI, no spot-squared: a legitimately DISTINCT semantic, and a local scalar never published as an exposure). strike_display_text.evidence: RC-325 scope repair 2026-08-26. This semantic existed TWICE — once in Python and once in JavaScript — while this gate reported PASS, because computing_sites counted definition sites only inside a corpus built from `git ls-files -- *.py`. MEASURED that day: the corpus held 222 files, 100% .py, while 19,224 tracked lines of production frontend were invisible to it, so a browser implementation incremented nothing and `len(sites) > 1` was unreachable across runtimes BY CONSTRUCTION. The browser copy is now deleted (static/js/strike_format.js removed, no surface references fmtStrike); the server computes the text and emits it (per-strike row index 3, and strike_labels on the terrain payload) and the surfaces render it. HARM the duplication caused, measured on the live CDE ladder (40 strikes): the browser rule produced 26 distinct labels — 14 real strikes erased by collision — and 16 of 40 named a price that does not trade.
